messages.subject: Order in parameters
parts:
I had the following in the parameters block:
real<lower=1/max(y), upper=1/min(y)> lambda[k];

I wish to impose the prior: 1(lambda[1]>lambda[2]>...>lambda[k]). I tried changing real to positive ordered to see if that did the trick. 3 out of chains certainly imposed this constraint and in the last one the order was reversed. What is the correct way of imposing this prior.

p.s. How can I tell stan lower=min(1/y). This chucks an error in stan and hence why I have used 1/max(y) instead.

Cheers,
Sachin

parts:
> On Nov 30, 2015, at 1:46 AM, Sachinthaka Abeywardana <sachin.ab...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I had the following in the parameters block:
> real<lower=1/max(y), upper=1/min(y)> lambda[k];
>
> I wish to impose the prior: 1(lambda[1]>lambda[2]>...>lambda[k]). I tried changing real to positive ordered to see if that did the trick. 3 out of chains certainly imposed this constraint and in the last one the order was reversed. What is the correct way of imposing this prior.
>
> p.s. How can I tell stan lower=min(1/y). This chucks an error in stan and hence why I have used 1/max(y) instead.

min and max should work the same way.

If you declare an ordered vector, all of the draws should
be ordered.

If that's not what's happening for you, could you please send
us a complete Stan program? It's hard to diagnose from fragments.

- Bob
